draft_notice: DRAFT for owner review, revised 2026-11-17 after an independent review of the fill rules. Nothing here is registered, no ledger exists, no trial has been claimed and no strategy return has been computed on real data. The only provider calls made were the data probe recorded under survivorship and data_feasibility: bar counts and time stamps for a few symbols and sessions. The runner refuses --acquire, --support-audit, --preflight and --fit while status is not 'registered'.

versions.long_only: PRIMARY, and the only decision. Takes only the buys: the selected names whose first five-minute bar closed above its open. Names whose first bar closed lower are skipped and their slots stay in cash. It must pass on its own, because the paper account has shorting disabled.
versions.long_short: SECONDARY, information only. The published strategy: the same buys plus a short sale of the selected names whose first bar closed lower, where the short rule under 'shorts' allows it. It is scored against the same criteria and its result is reported as secondary_decision. A long-short 'pass' while long-only fails permits nothing: no holdout check, no paper trading, no follow-up trial. It only records that the published form showed something in this window.

ledger_note: The experiment ledger permits exactly one hypothesis id per campaign, so the two versions are one registered trial with one claim. Both are scored in the same run from the same frozen data.
hypothesis: Each session, among US stocks with an opening price above 5 dollars, a 14-session average volume of at least 1,000,000 shares and a 14-session average true range above 0.50 dollars, the 20 with the highest first-five-minute volume relative to their own 14-session average for that window (at least 100 percent), bought (first bar closed up) or sold short (closed down) at the open of the one-minute bar after the first one that trades through the first five-minute bar's high or low, with a stop loss 10 percent of the average true range from the fill and an exit at the session close, earn more than cash after commission and 5 bps per side (both versions), and the long-only version earns more than a market position of the same size over the same minutes.

source.paper: Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz, 'A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market', Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper 24-98, SSRN 4729284 (2024). Read in full on 2026-11-17 from the University of St. Gallen repository copy; the rule below is taken from its sections 2, 2.1, 3 and 4.
source.published_rule: Filters: opening price above $5; average volume over the previous 14 days at least 1,000,000 shares a day; ATR over the previous 14 days above $0.50; Relative Volume at least 100 percent, where Relative Volume is the volume of the first 5 minutes divided by the mean first-5-minute volume of the previous 14 days; trade the top 20 by Relative Volume. If the first 5-minute candle closed above its open, a stop order to buy at the 5-minute high; below its open, a stop order to sell at the 5-minute low; a doji (open = close) places no order. A stop loss 10 percent of the 14-day ATR from the executed entry price. Positions not stopped are closed at 4:00 pm. Sized so that a stop-out loses 1 percent of the capital allocated to that position, with maximum leverage 4x. Commission $0.0035 per share; starting capital $25,000; January 2016 to December 2023.
source.published_result: Top-20 version: total return 1,637 percent, 41.6 percent a year, volatility 14.8 percent, Sharpe ratio 2.81, hit ratio 48.4 percent, worst day -1.61 percent, alpha 35.8 percent a year, beta 0.00 against the S&P 500. The same rule on every filtered stock without the relative-volume step: 3.2 percent a year, Sharpe 0.48.
source.published_data: Stock list from CRSP, stated free of survivorship bias; intraday data from IQFeed, unadjusted for splits and dividends. The paper states no slippage, no spread, no fill model beyond the stop price, and no borrow or short-sale constraint.
source.authors_interest: One author group. The first author runs Concretum Group, which sells research and trading tools; the third founded Bear Bull Traders, a day-trading education business, and Peak Capital Trading. No independent replication with realistic fills is known to us.

departures_from_the_paper: Fills. The paper fills a stop order at exactly its stop price and a stop loss at exactly its level. The deciding model here enters at the open of the next one-minute bar after the trigger and measures the stop from that fill; a stop-out fills at the stop price, or at the bar's open if the bar opens beyond it. Each side then pays a cost in basis points, which the paper does not charge. The paper's exact fills are scored beside it as an upper bound, and two harsher models as a required check and a lower bound.

Sizing. The paper's sentence is 'the loss on the capital allocated to that position would not exceed 1%' with 4x maximum leverage, and its footnote says the cap binds 'in some trades'. Read here as: each of the 20 names gets one twentieth of equity; a stop-out loses 1 percent of that slice (0.05 percent of equity); the position is capped at 4 times the slice. The owner's summary said 1 percent of equity; with 20 names and a 4x cap that reading would make the cap bind on every trade, which the footnote contradicts.

Universe. The paper uses the CRSP list including delisted stocks. Here the list is the broker's asset list (active and inactive), common stocks by an exchange-and-name proxy. The probe shows that list omits many delisted companies.

Shorts. The paper shorts every name. The long-short version here skips a short when the stock is under the short-sale price test or the broker's current flags say it cannot be borrowed easily; the paper's every-short version is reported only.
Primary version. The paper's strategy is long-short. Long-only is primary here because the account cannot short.
ATR. The paper says '14-day ATR' without the smoothing. Here it is the plain mean of the true range over the previous 14 sessions, which needs no earlier history.
Splits. Raw prices and volumes do not compare across a split. A name is not eligible from the split session through the next 14 sessions. The paper does not say how it handled this.
Halts. A position whose price record ends more than 30 minutes before the close is closed at the last print less one full average true range. The paper does not mention halts.
Window. 2016-01-04 to 2025-12-31, two years longer than the paper. The first 15 sessions only supply history.
Relative volume threshold. The paper says both 'at least 100%' and 'exceeded 100%'; 'at least' is used.
economic_motivation: A stock with unusually heavy volume at the open usually has company news. The paper argues that the direction of the first five minutes then shows which way large investors are leaning, and that the move tends to continue for the rest of the day. A tight stop keeps losses small on the days it does not.
distinct_from_consumed: An intraday breakout rule on a daily-changing set of single stocks chosen by opening volume. The consumed campaigns were an intraday model on three stocks (model_replacement_20260921, day_sleeve_horizon_trial_20261018), a 60-session price filter on six ETFs (research_reset_trend_20260908), a 63-session relative-strength rule on six ETFs (cross_sectional_momentum_trial_20261018), an SPY volatility target (volatility_target_core_trial_20261025), a 5-session sector-relative reversal in 300 stocks (swing_reversal_trial_20261115) and an SPY first-half-hour to last-half-hour rule (intraday_momentum_trial_20261115).

universe.rule: A candidate is a symbol of one to five letters on NYSE, NASDAQ or NYSE American in the broker's asset list (active or inactive) whose name does not match excluded_name_pattern: the swing trial's common-stock proxy. The pattern removes funds and, by name, American depositary receipts and shares (ADRs), warrants, units, rights and preferred shares. On session t a candidate passes if its raw daily open on t is above 5 dollars, its mean raw daily volume over sessions t-14 to t-1 is at least 1,000,000 shares, and the mean of its true range over sessions t-14 to t-1 is above 0.50 dollars. True range is the largest of high minus low, high minus the previous close, and the previous close minus low. All 15 daily bars from t-15 to t-1 must exist. Nothing from t except the open is used.
universe.split_guard: A name is not eligible on any session from a split's first session through the 14 sessions after it. Splits are found at acquisition as the sessions where the ratio of the raw close to the split-adjusted close changes by more than 1 percent, and frozen with a hash.
universe.shortlist: To avoid downloading daily bars for every symbol, daily bars are fetched only for candidates with at least one calendar month of raw volume of 7,000,000 shares or more and at least one monthly high above 5 dollars. A 14-session window averaging 1,000,000 shares lies inside at most two calendar months, so one of them has at least 7,000,000: no name that could pass is dropped.
universe.fidelity: These are the paper's three filters with the paper's numbers. The differences are the source of the stock list (see survivorship) and the common-stock proxy, which uses today's names and can misclassify in both directions.

signal.rule: The opening range is the provider's five-minute bar stamped 09:30 New York time (09:30:00 to 09:34:59). Relative volume on session t is that bar's volume on t divided by the mean of that bar's volume over sessions t-14 to t-1; the bar must exist on all 14; a name missing any of them is unranked until it has 14 in a row again. Among the names that pass the universe filters on t, those with relative volume of at least 1.0 are ranked highest first, ties by symbol, and the top 20 are selected. Direction: bar close above bar open is a buy; below is a sell; equal (a doji) keeps its rank and places no order. The selection uses nothing after 09:35 on t.
signal.computed_at_acquisition: The selection is computed once at acquisition from raw volumes and the opening bars, frozen with a hash, and rebuilt and compared before scoring. It decides which minute bars are downloaded. It contains no outcome.

trade.rule: At 09:35 the order for each selected name is armed at the opening bar's high (buy) or low (sell). It can trigger on any one-minute bar from the one stamped 09:35. Under the deciding fill model the trade is entered at the next bar's open. The stop loss is set 10 percent of the 14-session average true range away from the actual fill price, not from the trigger. If the stop loss is not reached the position is closed at the close of the last one-minute bar of the regular session (stamped 15:59, or 12:59 on an early close). One order per name per session; no re-entry; nothing is held overnight.

sizing.rule: Equity is divided into 20 equal slots, one per selected name. Shares = the smaller of (1 percent of the slot) / (stop distance in dollars) and (4 times the slot) / (trigger price), fixed when the order is placed. So a stop-out at exactly the stop price loses 0.05 percent of equity, a position is at most 20 percent of equity, and the whole book is at most 4 times equity. Unused slots stay in cash. Fractional shares are allowed, so the result does not depend on account size.
sizing.return_unit: Each session's return is the sum of that session's trade results divided by the equity at that morning. One observation per eligible session; a session with no fill is zero.
sizing.reported_only: Equal-notional sizing: every fill at the 4x cap (20 percent of equity), which is what the other reading of the paper ('a stop-out loses 1 percent of equity', capped at 4x for the book) reduces to. Reported for both versions; decides nothing.

models.bar_executable: DECIDES. Written for a buy; a short sale is the mirror image. The trigger bar is the first one-minute bar, from the one stamped 09:35, whose high reaches the opening bar's high. The trade is entered at the open of the NEXT one-minute bar, whatever that price is, above or below the trigger. If the trigger bar is the session's last bar there is no trade. The stop loss is 10 percent of the average true range below that fill. From the entry bar on: a bar that opens at or below the stop exits at its open; otherwise a bar whose low reaches the stop exits at the stop price. If neither happens the trade exits at the close of the last bar. Every price used is one the one-minute record shows in order, so the model neither keeps the good half nor the bad half of a minute's move.
models.conservative: MUST ALSO BE POSITIVE (mean net return at the base cost). The same entry. A bar whose low reaches the stop exits at the worse of the stop price and the next bar's open.
models.paper_exact: REPORTED ONLY, upper bound. Entry at exactly the trigger price. The trigger bar cannot stop the trade. A later bar whose low reaches the stop exits at exactly the stop price, gaps included.
models.lower_bound: REPORTED ONLY, lower bound: the first draft's rules. A gap through the trigger fills at the bar's open; a trigger bar whose low is a stop distance below the trigger counts as a stop-out; otherwise the entry is the worse of the trigger and the next bar's open; stop exits are the worse of the stop and the next bar's open.

fills.slippage: No slippage is built into the deciding fill prices. It is carried once, by the per-side cost.
fills.calibration: Synthetic only (scratch run 2026-11-17, 6,000 simulated days per setting, a random walk with no edge, more volatile at the open, mean result per fill in planned losses before costs, standard error 0.04 to 0.06). Calm to very volatile minutes: bar_executable -0.02, +0.01, +0.04, +0.09; conservative -0.10, -0.09, -0.14, -0.17; paper_exact +0.02, +0.06, +0.12, +0.21; lower_bound -0.20, -0.24, -0.44, -0.61. The deciding model is within about two standard errors of zero; it drifts slightly positive when minutes are very volatile, because a real stop fills a little beyond its price. The conservative model is still biased against the strategy by 0.1 to 0.2 planned losses, so the conservative criterion is a demanding one. A unit test (8,000 simulated days, fixed seed) fails if the deciding model scores a no-edge process outside plus or minus 0.10 planned losses per fill, or if the lower bound is not below -0.15; it measures +0.04 and -0.21, standard error 0.03.
fills.stale_rule: In every model, if a position's last bar is more than 30 minutes before the session close (a halt, or the record ends), it is closed at that last price moved against it by one full 14-session average true range, ten times the planned loss, but never below one cent.
fills.commission_note: $0.0035 per share per side, as in the paper. The broker's per-order minimum (about $0.35) is not charged, because results are stated per dollar of equity; on a $25,000 account it would add roughly 1 to 2 bps to small positions.

shorts.account_note: The paper account runs with shorting disabled, so the long-short version cannot be traded as configured today.
shorts.rule: A sell stop is taken in the long-short version only if all hold: (1) the frozen asset list marks the symbol shortable and easy to borrow (today's flags; an inactive symbol has neither, so delisted names are never shorted); (2) the stock did not fall 10 percent or more below its previous close on the prior session (the short-sale price test would still be in force); (3) the sell trigger is above 90 percent of the prior close (below that the price test would be in force before the order could fill). A blocked short leaves its slot in cash.
shorts.borrow_cost: None is charged: the position is opened and closed the same day, and stock-loan fees accrue on positions held overnight. Whether shares could have been located that morning is unknown.
shorts.reported_only: The same book with every sell stop taken, as the paper trades it, is reported and decides nothing.

data_probe.note: `--probe` asks for one-minute, five-minute and daily bars for each listed symbol and session and records bar counts and stamps only. The delisted list is large US companies acquired, merged or bankrupt between 2016 and 2023, each with a session on which it was trading.

survivorship.probe_finding: Probe run 2026-11-17 (artifacts/opening_range_trial_20261117/data_probe.json, bar counts and stamps only). For 21 large companies delisted between 2016 and 2023, each on a session when it was trading, the provider returned one-minute bars for all 21 and the opening five-minute bar for 20 (CERN did not trade in the first five minutes of that session). But only 10 of the 21 are in the broker's asset list (AGN, ALXN, CELG, CERN, EMC, RTN, SHLD, TIF, WLL, XLNX). BBBY, CHK, FRC, FTR, LNKD, MNK, MON, SIVB, TWTR, TWX and YHOO are absent, so a candidate list built from the asset list cannot include them. The bars exist; the names cannot be discovered. Symbols are also reused: EMC is listed as active, SHLD as both active and inactive, and a separate one-off check found daily bars for MON, EMC, SHLD and MNK a year after each stopped trading.
survivorship.label: incomplete_direction_unknown
survivorship.probe_status_values: Before registration set probe_status to 'delisted_symbols_served' or 'delisted_symbols_missing_or_partial'. The runner refuses any other value. With the second value the report labels every result 'incomplete_direction_unknown'.
survivorship.limits: A delisted company missing from the asset list never enters the candidate list, so its days are missing from the test, including the days around a takeover or a failure, when a stock is most 'in play'. Unlike a buy-the-losers rule, the direction of the resulting error is not known for a same-day breakout rule. No stress can cover names that never enter.
survivorship.extension_assessment: Assessed 2026-11-17 with a few lookups; nothing was built or downloaded. The provider serves bars for a delisted symbol if the symbol is asked for, so a list of delisted tickers with dates would extend the candidate set. Primary sources: SEC EDGAR Form 25 and 25-NSE filings record every removal from a US exchange with a date and are free and citable, but they identify the issuer (CIK and name), not reliably the ticker, and EDGAR's ticker file lists current tickers only; exchange notices (Nasdaq's daily list) cover one exchange and are not a bulk history. Free vendor lists carry ticker, name, exchange, type and delisting date in one file: Alpha Vantage's listing-status file (state=delisted), Financial Modeling Prep's delisted-companies list, EODHD's delisted exchange list, and stockanalysis.com's yearly tables. None is a primary record, their completeness cannot be audited without CRSP, and none of their contents were checked here. Index-constituent histories cover only the largest few hundred names. What it would take: one vendor file frozen with a hash; keep common stocks delisted in 2016-2025 on the three exchanges; add them to the candidates; cut each one's bars at its delisting date; one more owner decision. Bias that would remain: unknown gaps in the vendor list; reused tickers (the probe found EMC, SHLD, MON and MNK serving bars after the original company was gone), which the date cut reduces but does not remove when the reuse precedes the cut; renamed tickers counted as a delisting plus a new listing; no shortable flag and no name-based stock filter for symbols outside the broker's list. The label would stay 'incomplete_direction_unknown' with a smaller gap.

cost_tiers.name: half
cost_tiers.caveat: A result that holds at 2.5 bps but not at 5 bps is not established.

cost_tiers.name: commission_only_as_published
cost_tiers.caveat: The paper's cost assumption. With the paper_exact fill model this is the closest this runner gets to the published test. Decides nothing.

cost_basis: The per-side cost stands for half the quoted spread plus the slip of a stop order that becomes a market order in a fast stock. The bot's own fills (research note 'measured_costs_from_fills', 2026-11-15: 124 marketable one-to-two-share paper fills in AAPL, AMZN and MSFT, almost all midday) cost 0.9 bps on average against the mid, with a 90th percentile of 6 bps. The names traded here are not three giant stocks at midday: they are whichever stocks have the most unusual volume that morning, many priced between 5 and 30 dollars where one cent is 3 to 20 bps, in the first minutes after the open when spreads are widest, entered in the direction the price is already running. 5 bps per side is about the 90th percentile of the measured midday giant-stock cost, taken as the typical cost here, and decides. The strategy must still be positive at 7.5 bps. 10 bps, 2.5 bps and commission only are reported. None of these is measured for these stocks at this time of day.
cost_scale: Stated before any result. Per fill: a position is about 2 to 2.5 slots (10 to 12.5 percent of equity) when the daily range is 4 to 5 percent of the price, so a round trip at 5 bps per side costs 2 x 5 bps x 10 to 12.5 percent = 1.0 to 1.25 bps of equity. That is 0.2 to 0.25 of the planned loss of 5 bps of equity (1 percent of a slot). Per day: with 12 to 15 fills out of 20 names the cost is 12 to 19 bps of equity, about 15. The paper's published 41.6 percent a year is ln(1.416)/252 = 13.8 bps a day, after commission, with ideal fills and no spread. So the base cost alone is about as large as the whole published return. If the paper is right about its gross returns and wrong only in charging no spread, the long-short book nets about zero here and fails; long-only has about half the fills and, if the edge is symmetric, half the return, so the same ratio. A fail at this cost is the likely outcome even if the paper's arithmetic is right. A pass would need the bar-executable fills to do better than the paper's own, or costs lower than assumed.
cost_accounting: Each fill pays $0.0035 per share and per_side_bps of its value. A trade has two fills. Orders that never trigger cost nothing. No borrow fee. Cash earns nothing. The cost is charged once: the deciding fill prices carry no extra slippage.

controls.exposure_matched_market: For every fill: the SPY one-minute close at the exit minute over the SPY one-minute close at the entry minute, minus 1, times the position's signed weight. Summed per session. Charged no cost. The long-only comparison: it is what the same dollars would have earned in the market over the same minutes.

paired_difference: Per eligible session: the version's net return minus its exposure-matched market return.
observation_unit: One observation per eligible session, in calendar order for the block bootstrap.

session_rules.calendar: The exchange calendar is required; the runner refuses the rule-based fallback.
session_rules.eligible_session: A session is scored when it has 15 earlier sessions in the window and SPY has a one-minute bar for every minute of that session's regular hours. SPY trades every minute, so a gap means the provider's record of that session is incomplete or trading was halted market-wide; the session is skipped and counted. This is expected to drop the four market-wide circuit-breaker days of March 2020 (9, 12, 16 and 18), which were among the most volatile sessions in the window; the support audit will show the count.
session_rules.early_closes: Traded like any other session, with the exit at the early close (the bar stamped 12:59). Bars stamped at or after the session's close are discarded.
session_rules.sparse_bars: A stock has no one-minute bar for a minute with no trade. That is normal and is not a gap. A selected name with no bar at all from 09:35 on gets no order.

support_rationale: The exchange calendar has 2,514 development sessions; less the first 15 that leaves at most 2,499 eligible days, 237 in 2016 and 250 to 252 in later years. The thresholds allow about 8 percent of days to be lost and one thin year. The median eligible day must have at least 10 selected names, half the 20 slots. Each version must also fill at least 5,000 trades (about two a day); this depends on prices, so it is checked only after the claim.

support_audit.rule: `--support-audit` reads sessions, symbols and bar times only and writes artifacts/opening_range_trial_20261117/support_audit.json with prices_read_for_analysis=false and strategy_outcomes_computed=false. A failed audit blocks without consuming the trial.

acceptance.long_only_summary: All of, under the bar_executable fill model unless stated: adequate support; the bootstrap lower bound of the mean net return per eligible session at 5 bps per side is above zero; the mean net return is above zero at 7.5 bps per side; the mean net return at 5 bps is above zero under the conservative fill model; the mean net return at 5 bps is above zero in at least 6 of the 10 calendar years; the bootstrap lower bound of the mean paired difference against the exposure-matched market at 5 bps is above zero.
acceptance.long_short_summary: Information only. The same criteria except the market comparison, which is reported. Whatever its result it permits nothing; see versions.long_short.
acceptance.reported_only: The 10 bps, 2.5 bps and commission-only tiers; the paper_exact and lower_bound fill models and the conservative model's full figures; the every-short-taken book; equal-notional sizing; the paired difference for long-short; Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, annualized percent, hit ratio, average result in planned losses, exit reasons, gap entries, order statuses, shorts blocked, commission per day, turnover and per-year figures.
acceptance.pass_means: Long-only pass: in 2016-2025, entering at the next minute's open after the breakout and after commission and 5 bps per side, the buy side of the rule made money by a margin a block bootstrap separates from zero, in most years, still made money at 7.5 bps and under the conservative fills, and beat the same dollars held in SPY over the same minutes by a margin the bootstrap also separates from zero. It permits one check on the untouched holdout and, if that agrees, at least eight weeks on the paper account. It does not permit real-money trading.
acceptance.long_short_pass_means: Nothing is permitted. If long-short meets its criteria while long-only does not, the trial is retired and the report records that the published long-short form showed a result in this window. Any later test of a shortable version would be a new hypothesis under a new contract.
acceptance.fail_means: Retired: the data were adequate and at least one long-only criterion failed. Both versions end; no tuning of filters, the opening range length, the number of names, the stop, sizing, fill model, costs or acceptance follows. Inconclusive: support was inadequate after the claim; the budget is still consumed.

multiple_testing: This contract tests two hypotheses, so each bootstrap lower bound is the 1.25th percentile (a 97.5 percent two-sided interval) instead of the 2.5th. By the intraday contract's count nine earlier hypotheses were tested and none passed, so a pass here would be the first in eleven attempts on overlapping data; at this threshold the chance of at least one false pass in eleven is roughly 13 percent. That is why a pass leads to one untouched holdout check and paper trading, not to real money.

parameter_justifications.signal.opening_range_minutes=5: The paper's headline version; it also reports 15, 30 and 60 minutes, which are not tested here.
parameter_justifications.sizing.risk_fraction_of_slot=0.01, max_l: The paper's numbers under the slot reading; see departures_from_the_paper.
parameter_justifications.fills.stale_exit_minutes=30, stale_exit_: Thirty minutes without a print near the close in a stock chosen for heavy volume means a halt or a broken record. One average true range is ten times the planned loss and about the size of a normal day's range; halts on news can move more.
Rule 201 of Regulation SHO: after a 10 percent fall from the prior close, short sales may not hit the bid for the rest of that day and the next.
parameter_justifications.adjustment=raw: The paper uses unadjusted intraday data. The 5 dollar and 1,000,000 share filters only mean what they say on the prices and volumes of the day; split-adjusted data would shrink past prices of stocks that later split. Within a session raw and adjusted returns are identical.
parameter_justifications.acceptance.minimum_positive_years=6: A majority of ten years, as in the earlier contracts.
parameter_justifications.support_thresholds: About 92 percent of the possible days and nine of ten years, as in the intraday contract; see support_rationale.
parameter_justifications.bootstrap.block_days=21: One trading month of daily observations, as in the intraday contract: bursts of news-driven volume (earnings seasons, 2020, 2021) cluster for weeks.
parameter_justifications.bootstrap.replicates=10000, lower_quanti: The earlier contracts' values: Bonferroni for two hypotheses at a 5 percent two-sided level.
parameter_justifications.fills.deciding_model=bar_executable: One-minute bars cannot show the order of prices inside a bar. A model that fills inside the trigger bar must guess, and each pessimistic guess keeps the bad half of a minute's move: on a simulated walk with no edge the first draft's rules scored -0.2 to -0.6 planned losses per fill before costs. Entering at the next bar's open uses only prices whose order is known, and scores the same walk at about zero. The cost is fidelity: the paper enters at the trigger itself, typically a little earlier and at a different price.
parameter_justifications.fills.required_positive_model=conservati: A real stop order in a fast stock often fills beyond its price. The conservative model charges that by taking the next bar's open when it is worse. It is biased against the strategy (about -0.1 to -0.2 planned losses per fill on a no-edge walk), so it is required only to be positive in the mean, not to clear the bootstrap.
parameter_justifications.cost_tiers=5/7.5 decide; 10/2.5/0 report: See cost_basis and cost_scale. The stress level is one and a half times the base: at double the base the cost would exceed the paper's whole published return, so that level is reported, not required.

data_feasibility.measured: Run 2026-11-17 against the provider; counts, stamps and timings only. (1) One-minute and five-minute raw SIP bars exist from the first session of the window, 2016-01-04, for all 5 coverage symbols on all 5 probed sessions. SPY and AAPL had a bar for every regular minute (390, or 210 on the 2019-11-29 early close). BLDR, KBH and PLUG had 335 to 390 of 390, because a minute with no trade has no bar. (2) The 09:30 five-minute bar equalled its one-minute bars (volume, high, low) in all 25 cases. (3) Bars stamped after an early close exist and must be discarded. (4) One request returned the 09:30 bar for 300 symbols in 0.4 seconds and for 757 symbols in 0.65 seconds; one request returned a full session of minute bars for 20 symbols (7,627 bars) in 0.24 seconds; a month of SPY minute bars (15,936 including extended hours) took 0.3 to 0.6 seconds. (5) The provider's rate-limit header reads 200 requests a minute, and the running bot draws on the same allowance. (6) A five-minute request spanning several days returns every bar, not just the 09:30 one, so opening bars are requested one session at a time.
data_feasibility.plan: From Alpaca, SIP feed, raw: (1) the asset list; (2) monthly bars for every candidate, to shortlist; (3) daily bars for the shortlist, raw and split-adjusted; (4) the 09:30 five-minute bar, one request per session per 500 names, for every name that passes the daily filters that session or in the next 14; (5) one-minute bars from 09:35 to the close for the selected names, one request per session; (6) SPY one-minute bars, one request per month.
data_feasibility.estimate: Inferred, not measured. Sizes come from the swing trial's frozen monthly bars: 6,294 candidates; about 4,600 shortlisted; about 700 to 1,450 names a month pass the price and volume filters before the range filter (median about 960). Requests: about 110 for monthly bars, about 1,700 pages of daily bars (about 8.4 million rows, fetched raw and split-adjusted), about 7,500 for opening bars (2 to 3 per session), about 2,500 for minute bars, about 240 pages for SPY: about 12,000 in all. At the runner's pace of about 100 a minute that is 2 to 3 hours. Rows kept: about 8.4 million daily, 2.5 to 3.5 million opening bars, at most 19 million stock minute bars (20 names x 385 minutes x 2,499 sessions; fewer in practice), 0.98 million SPY minute bars. Disk: roughly 0.4 to 0.6 GB as gzip CSV (70 GB are free). Memory: the machine has 3 GB with about 1 GB free while the bot runs; the runner works one symbol chunk and one month at a time to stay inside that, which has been exercised on synthetic data only.
data_feasibility.why_not_everything: One-minute bars for every filtered stock on every day would be about 1,000 names x 390 bars x 2,514 sessions, about a billion rows. The selection needs only the first five-minute bar, and only the 20 selected names need their minute path, which cuts the download to about 2 percent of that without changing a single trade.
data_feasibility.memory: Measured on synthetic data, 2026-11-17: the selection step on 3.67 million opening bars for 3,000 names over 2,514 sessions, read month by month from gzip files, with 1.21 million filter rows, peaked at 515 MB for the whole process (140 MB of that is the program's imports). The first draft built a sessions-by-names table and peaked at 1,641 MB on 3.4 million bars. A unit test bounds the step at 100 bytes per opening bar (64 measured). The acquisition holds the filter rows and one month of bars at a time; that path has been run end to end only on a small synthetic market.

acquisition: Not done. After registration and on the owner's word only, `--acquire` runs once, needs the Alpaca data credentials, pauses 0.6 seconds per page so it uses about half the shared rate limit, and retries a transient error up to four times. It refuses, writing no manifest: any row dated outside development or in 2026; monthly or daily fetch failures for more than 1 percent of the symbols asked for; split-adjusted daily bars that do not cover exactly the raw daily bars (the split guard depends on them); on ANY single session, opening-bar failures for more than 1 percent of the names asked for that session, or opening bars returned for fewer than 90 percent of them; selected names without minute bars above 1 percent of all orders; an incomplete SPY minute record on more than 1 percent of sessions. Every session's opening-bar counts (asked, returned, failed) are written to the manifest. It refuses to overwrite an existing acquisition. It should be run outside market hours, because the running bot uses the same rate limit.
availability_check: data probe only (2026-11-17): bar counts and stamps for 5 symbols on 5 sessions and 21 delisted symbols on one session each; no price was kept and no return was computed
preconditions: owner approves these written rules before any result exists
the independent review's findings on the revised fill model, acquisition checks and memory are closed
owner adopts a research-reset amendment and config/research_reset.json registered_trials cites this campaign_id
status set to registered, draft_notice removed, and the contract registered under artifacts/opening_range_trial_20261117/campaign_state.json before any price is read for scoring
owner approves the one-time acquisition; manifest written with source hashes
non-claiming preflight passes: source hashes, 2016-2025 date bounds, no 2026 row, price validity, the frozen selection equals the selection rebuilt from the frozen bars
stop_rule: Claim once immediately before scoring; no retry after a claim, even after a crash. A failed support audit or preflight blocks without consuming the trial. A failed or inconclusive result retires both versions and authorizes no tuning of any parameter, fill model, cost or acceptance rule.
holdout_policy: 2026-09-09 to 2026-12-08 is not read during development. It is reserved as the single final check if the long-only version passes: about 60 sessions, scored once with these rules unchanged, as a consistency check that cannot establish significance. If it agrees, at least eight weeks on the paper account follow before any further decision.
execution_assumption: A simulation of orders on one-minute bars with a fixed fill model and fixed costs. It is not a record of fills. Order-book depth, queue position, the bot's own effect on price, trading halts shorter than the stale rule, and whether shares could be borrowed are not modelled.
limitations: One author group with a commercial interest in day-trading tools and education; no independent replication with realistic fills is known to us.
The published sample is eight years, 2016 to 2023, which contains the 2020-2021 retail-trading boom. Two more years are added here.

The published result assumes every stop order fills exactly at its price with no spread, and a stop only 10 percent of a day's range from entry. At the base cost the trading costs are about as large as the paper's whole published daily return (see cost_scale). A fail is therefore the likely outcome even if the paper's arithmetic is right, and would mean the edge does not survive plausible trading costs.

One-minute bars cannot show what happened inside a minute. The deciding model avoids the question by entering at the next minute's open, which is not what the paper trades: it enters later and at a different price. The paper's own fills and two harsher models are reported beside it.
The stock list comes from the broker's asset list, which omits many delisted companies; see survivorship. The paper's list included them.
The common-stock proxy uses today's names and exchanges. Shortable flags are today's.
Results are per dollar of equity with fractional shares. On a small account, minimum commissions and whole shares would cost more; on a large one, the bot's own orders would move these stocks.
The 4x intraday leverage in the sizing rule needs a margin account with pattern-day-trader status (at least $25,000).
Earlier research viewed SPY for 2016-2025 and three of these stocks for 2024-2025; the window is not untouched.

acquisition_thresholds.opening_bar_coverage_floor: 0.90 of the names asked for on one session (constant MIN_OPENING_COVERAGE). Every name asked for has a daily bar that session, so it traded; a missing opening bar means no trade between 09:30 and 09:35, which is rare for names averaging a million shares a day. In the probe 599 of 600 current liquid names returned the bar. An outage returns far fewer. Ten percent leaves room for halted opens.
acquisition_thresholds.failure_fraction: 0.01 (constants MAX_FAILED_FETCH_FRACTION and MAX_INCOMPLETE_SESSION_FRACTION), each in its own units as listed under acquisition.
